title: Mother of man fatally shot by police says \'nothing else\' police could have done, ASIRT clears officers
subtitle: Fatal shooting in southeast Calgary was recorded by CPS officers' body-worn cameras.
article: Calgary\'s police watchdog has cleared officers of wrongdoing in the fatal shooting of a man during a domestic disturbance call last month, citing body-worn camera footage and witness testimony from the man\'s mother as key evidence that the officer acted in self-defence.
The shooting occurred Feb. 19 as officers responded to a domestic disturbance call around 10:30 a.m. at a mobile home park in the 6200 block of 17th Avenue S.E.
In a report on its investigation into the incident, the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) says the mother of the man indicated she had a feeling about such an outcome.

In its report, ASIRT says officers were responding to a call from the sister of the man, expressing concerns about her brother\'s treatment of their elderly mother. While en route to the scene, an officer phoned the mother and learned that her son was displaying extreme anger and had access to a large dagger.

When police arrived, the man moved quickly toward an officer while holding a dagger in a threatening manner, according to the news release. The officer gave verbal commands to drop the weapon, but they were ignored. In response, the officer fired his service weapon, striking the man.
Despite immediate medical attention, he was declared dead at the scene, the report states.
ASIRT\'s investigation determined that the officer acted in self-defence.
The report states the mother indicated that "she knew something like this was going to happen."
"She had heard (her son) talk about dying at the hands of the police and she believed (he) was waiting for this to occur," the report states.
ASIRT says the mother asked for a message to be communicated to the officers involved: "She stated, \'I forgive him. He had to do his own job and there\'s nothing else he could\'ve done.\' "
The report also highlighted the role of body-worn camera footage in the investigation.
The fatality was the first officer-involved shooting in the city this year.
